feature.title: Cubes enhanced graphics
feature.request: Similar to how we added enhanced graphics to the dancing-character, I also want to add enhanced graphics to the cubes visualization. Ideate ways to enhance this visualization

problem.statement: The cubes visualizer is one InstancedMesh of glass MeshPhysicalMaterial cubes lit by a RoomEnvironment and three lights, rendered with a plain renderer.render and no post-processing. It looks flat next to what the dancer's planned enhanced mode will offer, and its beat reactions are limited to scale, colour, a bass bump and a background pulse. Users who want a richer show have no opt-in upgrade.
users: Listeners who open /cubes with an audio source and want a more spectacular, music-driven scene
Users on mid-range laptops with integrated graphics who must keep a smooth frame rate
evidence: app/features/visualizers/cubes/useCubesScene.ts:49-224 plain render, RoomEnvironment and PMREM at 0.3, key/fill/ambient lights
docs/plans/dancer-enhanced-graphics/dancer-enhanced-graphics.plan.md app-wide enhanced toggle, off by default, lazy EnhancedLook
app/features/visualizers/bass-ink/bassInkPost.ts the only post stack in the app

goals: An opt-in enhanced cubes look that is a clear visual upgrade: post-processing, richer lighting and materials, and new audio-driven elements
Enhanced mode exposed exactly like the dancer's enhanced graphics (one app-wide toggle, off by default)
Enhanced mode holds 60 fps on integrated graphics at 1080p
Basic mode unchanged in look, cost and bundle
non_goals: Changing the basic cubes look or its controls' behaviour
Implementing the dancer's enhanced mode (only sharing its toggle)
Upgrading three.js or adding a post-processing library outside three/addons
Per-device automatic quality detection or multi-level presets
Changing the rhythm or analyser DSP
success_metrics: Enhanced median fps at least 60 and p5 at least 50 over 60 s of playback on an integrated-GPU laptop at 1080p (PerformanceStats)
cubes.out reaction delay median within one frame (16.7 ms) of basic mode (debug:viz)
Initial Total JS stays within the .size-limit.json budget; enhanced code ships in a lazy chunk
Zero new console errors or WebGL context warnings in e2e
constraints: three.js r186 pinned; effects only from three/addons (AGENTS.md:59)
No allocation per frame; every GPU resource disposed; effects return cleanup (AGENTS.md:118-120)
Logic in classes and pure functions; scene reads changing values through refs (AGENTS.md:112-117)
Reuse useThreeScene (its render hook for post), createOrbitView, disposeScene, useControlValues and ControlPanel
Total JS gzip budget 348.5 kB (.size-limit.json:22); Lighthouse budget on / only
e2e runs software WebGL, CPU-bound, one worker; fixtures fail on WebGL context warnings (e2e/fixtures.ts:30)
95% coverage over app/**; new cubes controls change the settings-panel visual baseline

decisions.question: What should enhanced graphics for Cubes optimize for?
decisions.answer: A bigger visual upgrade: new elements (environment, particles, camera moves, new beat reactions) are in scope, not only polish of the existing look.
decisions.rationale: User chose the bigger upgrade over same-identity polish.

decisions.question: How is the enhanced mode exposed?
decisions.answer: The same way the dancing-character's enhanced graphics are exposed, for consistency across visualizers.

decisions.question: What is the performance floor?
decisions.answer: Enhanced mode holds 60 fps on integrated graphics of a mid laptop at 1080p; the basic mode is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the visualizer usable on common hardware.

decisions.question: What exact toggle does the dancer use?
decisions.answer: One app-wide setting in localStorage (key audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphics), off by default, that loads an enhanced module lazily and rebuilds the scene through useThreeScene.
decisions.rationale: docs/plans/dancer-enhanced-graphics plan D1/D2; the dancer code is not built yet.

decisions.question: Who builds the shared toggle if the dancer has not shipped it yet?
decisions.answer: One shared app-wide toggle for all visualizers; whichever plan lands first builds it as a shared module, the other reuses it.
decisions.rationale: User chose one shared toggle in round 2.

decisions.question: Which new elements are in emphasis?
decisions.answer: All four: glow and post FX, environment (floor, fog, backdrop), motion and camera (beat-synced moves, grid waves, shattering), and particles.
decisions.rationale: User selected all four in round 2; options must weigh them against the 60 fps floor.

decisions.question: Is the framing confirmed?
decisions.answer: Yes, as recorded in problem, goals, non-goals and ACs.

decisions.question: Where do the shared store, hook and toggle UI live?
decisions.answer: Exactly where the dancer plan puts them: app/features/settings/enhancedGraphicsStore.ts and useEnhancedGraphics.ts, with its signatures and its toggle UI. If cubes lands first, S1 builds that module and that UI as the dancer plan specifies, so there is one store and one surface.

decisions.question: Rebuild the scene or swap in place on toggle?
decisions.answer: Swap in place: useCubesScene holds the current look in a ref, and SceneHandle.render (read per frame, useThreeScene.ts:106) delegates to it. useThreeScene is unchanged, with no new renderer, context or camera reset.
decisions.rationale: Delivers the no-gap swap and keeps the camera pose (critic F2).

decisions.question: Reference device and fps cut list
decisions.answer: The reference device is the user's own integrated-GPU laptop at 1080p. A miss on AC3 is cut in this order: particle count, shatter term, composer pixel ratio 1, quarter-resolution bloom, opaque emissive material.
decisions.rationale: Pre-agreed cuts make each slice's AC3 re-check actionable (critic F4).

decisions.question: How do camera moves coexist with OrbitControls?
decisions.answer: The motion is applied to a scene-root group that holds the grid, floor and particles, never to camera.position, so orbit state, reset view and the view-changed flag are untouched.

options.summary: A lazy cubesEnhanced chunk reusing the shared app-wide toggle adds one bloom post pass, a fog/floor backdrop and one instanced spark-particle burst on kicks, leaving basic code paths untouched.
approach: Use the shared enhancedGraphics toggle (localStorage audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphics, off by default); build it as a shared module only if the dancer has not yet shipped it (D5).
In useCubesScene, when the toggle is off, run exactly today's code path; when on, dynamic-import ~/features/visualizers/cubes/enhanced/cubesEnhanced with an AbortSignal and rebuild via useThreeScene.

cubesEnhancedPost.ts: class modelled on bassInkPost (EffectComposer, RenderPass, single half-resolution UnrealBloomPass, OutputPass); exposed through the SceneHandle.render hook; idempotent dispose().
cubesBackdrop.ts: fog plus a reflective-looking dark floor plane (cheap MeshStandardMaterial, no mirror pass), tinted by bgPulse.
cubesSparks.ts: one preallocated InstancedMesh or Points pool (about 300) emitted on the existing cubesBass kick flash; ring-buffer, zero per-frame allocation; one draw call.
Camera: small beat-synced dolly nudge driven by the existing bass level; skipped under prefers-reduced-motion, and bloom strength is damped so there are no flashes (AC8).
Unit tests mock the addons (as in bassInkPost.test.ts) and assert dispose; extend the e2e round-trip context test; no new controls, so the settings-panel baseline is unchanged.

options.summary: A lazily loaded CubesEnhancedLook class owns a budgeted post stack (bloom, vignette), env and floor, a single instanced particle pool and beat-driven grid waves, driven by a pure CubesFxState and gated by one shared app-wide toggle with an AbortSignal-guarded rebuild, idempotent disposal and a reduced-motion damper.
approach: Shared toggle: if absent, build app/features/enhanced/enhancedGraphics.ts (localStorage key audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphics, default off, useSyncExternalStore hook, storage event); reuse if the dancer landed first.

useCubesScene reads the flag, and on true dynamic-imports cubesEnhanced.ts with an AbortSignal. Late or failed loads fall back to the basic look with a single logged warning, and the scene rebuilds through useThreeScene deps so the toggle needs no reload.

cubesFxState.ts (pure): maps band levels, bass flash and beat to wave phase, bloom strength, particle emit rate and camera nudge. All values are preallocated and clamped, and reduced-motion zeroes the camera and flash terms.

cubesPost.ts, modelled on bassInkPost: EffectComposer at a capped pixel ratio, RenderPass, a half-resolution UnrealBloomPass and OutputPass, with no afterimage pass. It exposes render(), setSize() and an idempotent dispose().

cubesEnhanced.ts: a CubesEnhancedLook class that adds a reflective floor, fog, a backdrop gradient and one Points or InstancedMesh particle pool (fixed count, ring-buffer recycling). It applies grid wave offsets to the existing instance matrices through a hook in cubeGrid.update. It returns dispose(), which frees the post stack, geometries, materials and textures.
Perf guard: fixed particle and bloom budgets set at build time, and a dev-only frame-time log through PerformanceStats. Measure on integrated graphics and tune the constants (no auto quality tiers).

Tests: unit tests for the fx state, the post class (addons mocked) and dispose counts; an e2e toggle round-trip checking context count and console; a debug:viz delay comparison; a size-limit check on the new chunk.

options.summary: Break the assumption that enhanced means adding layers on top of the glass look: swap the costly transparent glass for opaque emissive cubes in enhanced mode, spend the recovered fill-rate on one half-res bloom plus GPU-driven shader effects (no CPU particles, no extra passes).
approach: Shared toggle (audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphics, D4/D5) read in useCubesScene; when on, dynamic import of cubes/enhanced/enhancedCubes chunk, scene rebuilt via useThreeScene with an AbortSignal for late loads.

Enhanced cube material: opaque MeshStandardMaterial with per-instance emissive driven by band level (onBeforeCompile adds beat-wave term); removes 1800+ blended overdraw layers, the main iGPU cost of the glass look.
Grid waves and shatter are vertex-shader terms: uniforms (beat phase, bass flash, band levels) written from existing cubesBass/bands values; zero extra CPU per cube.
Particles: one THREE.Points with a GPU-only vertex shader (position from time + seed + bass uniform); fixed buffer, no per-frame allocation.
Post: EffectComposer with RenderPass, one UnrealBloomPass at half resolution, OutputPass (pattern from bassInkPost.ts); no afterimage. Plain floor and fog added as cheap opaque mesh and scene.fog.
Camera drift and flash intensity multiplied by a reduced-motion factor (matchMedia) for AC8.
Class EnhancedCubesLook with update(frame) and idempotent dispose(); basic path untouched.

options.summary: O2's structure (shared toggle, AbortSignal loader, pure CubesFxState, idempotent dispose) with O3's no-gap swap, load-failure fallback and enhanced-only controls, and O4's GPU-side effects (vertex-shader grid waves and shatter, shader-driven particles) so the upgrade covers glow, environment, motion and particles inside the 60 fps budget. Glass stays unless measurement forces O4's opaque emissive material.
approach: Shared toggle from the dancer plan (D4/D5): build app-wide useEnhancedGraphics if it is absent, reuse it otherwise.

useCubesScene takes an additive enhanced option. When it is on, loadCubesEnhanced(signal) dynamic-imports the lazy chunk while the basic look keeps rendering, then swaps. Late loads are aborted; a failed load keeps the basic look and shows one role=status notice.

CubesEnhancedLook (class) owns an EffectComposer with RenderPass, a half-resolution UnrealBloomPass and OutputPass (the bassInkPost pattern) through the SceneHandle.render hook. It also owns a dark glossy floor, exponential fog and a backdrop gradient.

A pure CubesFxState maps band levels, the cubesBass flash and beat phase from useRhythm to uniforms: wave phase, shatter amount, bloom strength, particle emit and camera nudge. Values are preallocated and clamped, and the reduced-motion factor zeroes camera and flash terms.

GPU effects: a cloned enhanced cube material with an onBeforeCompile vertex term for grid ripples and a bass-drop shatter offset. One THREE.Points layer is positioned in its vertex shader from seed, time and the bass uniform. No per-cube CPU work and no per-frame allocation.
Camera: a beat-synced dolly and orbit drift layered on createOrbitView, off under prefers-reduced-motion.
An enhanced-only ControlPanel group (Glow, Particles, Camera motion) shows only when enhanced is on, so the default settings-panel baseline is unchanged.
A measurement gate on an integrated GPU after the post and environment slice: if AC3 fails with glass, swap the enhanced cube material to O4's opaque emissive variant before adding more effects.

decision_rationale: O1 scores highest on cost but delivers only bloom, a floor and sparks: no grid waves, shatter or camera moves, so it misses the bigger upgrade (D1) and the four-way emphasis (D6). O5 keeps O1's bassInkPost-based post stack and lazy chunk, adds O2's testable pure state and abort/dispose discipline, O3's seamless swap and failure fallback, and O4's GPU-side effects. That reaches every emphasis area at near-zero CPU cost, with a measurement gate that falls back to O4's opaque material if glass misses 60 fps.

design.overview: Basic cubes stays on its current path. When the shared enhanced flag is on, useCubesScene lazy-loads a cubes/enhanced chunk and swaps a CubesEnhancedLook in place: the SceneHandle.render hook delegates to the look held in a ref, on the same renderer and context. The look owns a bloom post stack (EffectComposer, RenderPass, half-res UnrealBloomPass, OutputPass using the renderer's existing tone mapping and output colour space, with enhanced-only light constants retuned), a floor, fog and backdrop, a material it applies to the grid through a narrow CubeGrid API with GPU wave and shatter terms, a shader-driven particle layer, and beat motion on a scene-root group. A pure CubesFxState turns analyser, cubesBass and useRhythm signals (nullable phases) into uniforms through refs, with the reduced-motion damper built in from S2. Each slice re-checks AC3 on the reference device against D10's cut list.

design.data: One localStorage boolean (shared). No other persisted data; enhanced controls use useControlValues like the existing ones.
design.ux: The toggle is the dancer plan's shared setting and surface (D8). On /cubes, flipping it on keeps the basic look until the chunk arrives, then swaps on the same canvas. Flipping it off swaps back at once, and the camera pose is kept. An Enhanced control group (Glow, Particles, Camera motion) appears only while enhanced is on. A failed load keeps the basic look and shows a short role=status notice beside the cubes control panel.
design.accessibility: prefers-reduced-motion (matchMedia, live) zeroes camera moves and clamps bloom spikes and shatter so no full-screen flashes occur (AC8). The notice is role=status; new controls use the existing accessible ControlPanel.
design.security_privacy: No new data, network or permissions; only a same-origin lazy chunk.
design.observability: PerformanceStats fps in dev; debug:viz cubes telemetry compares reaction delay between modes; one console.warn (not error) on a failed chunk load.
design.rollout: Ships off by default behind the shared toggle; rollback is turning the flag off or reverting the PR. Visual baselines for the default mode stay unchanged.

test_strategy.unit: cubesFxState: clamps, the reduced-motion damper, null phases and barLocked false give zero amplitude, no allocation (same output object). loadCubesEnhanced: resolves ok:false on abort and on import failure. CubesEnhancedLook with mocked addons (the bassInkPost.test.ts pattern): attach and re-attach after a grid rebuild, and dispose once and idempotently. CubeGrid.setMaterialOverride sets and restores the material. The store and hook follow the dancer plan's tests. Shader chunks get uniform-shape and compile smoke tests, not text snapshots. Keep 95% coverage.
test_strategy.integration: useCubesScene with the fake renderer: enhanced=false never constructs a composer or calls setMaterialOverride. A toggle round trip keeps one renderer and restores the glass material. A resize with enhanced on re-attaches without stale meshes. With the flag off, the settings panel matches today's and the hidden enhanced controls do not affect basic mode. The failed-load notice renders as role=status.
test_strategy.e2e: A new spec seeds localStorage enhanced=true. /cubes renders one canvas that is not blank (pixel statistics), with one enhanced visual baseline. A toggle round trip keeps the same canvas and context count. A viewport resize, a source switch and a route round trip release the context. The lazy chunk is requested only when enabled. No console errors or WebGL warnings. Existing default-mode baselines are unchanged.
test_strategy.manual: npm run dev on the reference laptop at 1080p. Record basic fps first, then after each slice record 60 s of a 128 BPM track with PerformanceStats (median 60, p5 50, frame-time p95 at most 20 ms). Also check an unlocked camera drag during playback, OS reduced motion, silence and no source.
test_strategy.non_functional: npm run size in S1 records the gzip total and the delta, checks the entry and Total JS lines, and confirms the post addons share a chunk with bass-ink. debug:viz --viz cubes compares the envelope in both modes. Lighthouse on / is unaffected.

risks.description: Bloom over transparent glass with 1800+ instances misses 60 fps on integrated GPUs
risks.mitigation: Record basic fps first, then re-check AC3 after every slice. Run the opaque-emissive spike in S2 so the glass-or-opaque choice rests on a measurement, and apply D10's cut list on any miss.

risks.description: The composer adds render latency that the cubes.out envelope probe cannot see

open_questions.question: Confirm the reference integrated-GPU laptop (D10 assumes the user's own) before S2's measurement.

findings.finding: C1, K3 and D5 claim the shared toggle is 'identical to the dancer plan', but the dancer plan (docs/plans/dancer-enhanced-graphics/dancer-enhanced-graphics.plan.json) puts the store and hook in app/features/settings/ (enhancedGraphicsStore.ts, useEnhancedGraphics.ts), with several signatures in its options (boolean vs [boolean, setter]). This plan creates app/features/enhanced/enhancedGraphics.ts. If cubes lands first there are two stores on one localStorage key. The dancer plan also hides the toggle UI in production behind ENHANCED_GRAPHICS_UI until its S3, and Q1 (where the toggle lives) is non-blocking. So if cubes lands first, AC2 and AC4 ('the user flips the toggle') have no UI surface in production.
findings.suggestion: Adopt the dancer plan's final path and signature in C1 (app/features/settings/...). Say what S1 does when the module is absent: build exactly that module, and either include a minimal toggle UI or state that /cubes is reachable only by localStorage seed or in dev until the dancer UI lands. Make Q1 blocking for S1.
findings.resolution: Changed: C1 and D8 adopt the dancer plan's app/features/settings path, signatures and toggle UI. S1 builds exactly that if absent, so there is one store and one surface. Q1 removed, since D8 settles it.

findings.finding: The swap mechanism contradicts itself. useThreeScene (app/hooks/useThreeScene.ts:49-125) builds once; its effect deps are [containerRef, antialias] and setup is read through a ref. A toggle rebuild therefore needs a new dep (the dancer plan abuses antialias), but app/hooks/useThreeScene.ts is not in any slice's draft_paths. A rebuild also makes a new renderer, canvas and context, and rebuilds the PMREM environment and orbit view. That is incompatible with 'keeps rendering the basic look while the chunk loads, then swaps, with no blank frame' and loses camera pose and the reset-view state. The alternative, mutating the returned handle.render in place (read per frame at :106), is not what C5, AC4 or the K5 mitigation describe.
findings.suggestion: Pick one mechanism in the plan. In-place swap: the handle gets a mutable look, with the e2e context-count test asserting no new context. Or rebuild: add an explicit useThreeScene option, list the file in S1, keep the camera pose in a ref, and drop the 'no gap' claim from the UX text.
findings.resolution: Changed: D9 picks an in-place swap through a ref behind SceneHandle.render. useThreeScene is unchanged. AC4 and C5 now say same canvas and context, and e2e asserts the context count.

findings.finding: Hidden coupling to CubeGrid. C3 passes `grid` to the look's constructor and promises to 'restore the grid material', but useCubesScene's resize() (useCubesScene.ts:167-179) disposes the grid and builds a new CubeGrid on any window-size change that alters rows or columns. The look would then hold a disposed grid and a cloned onBeforeCompile material whose instances are gone. CubeGrid.material is private (cubeGrid.ts:44) and cubeGrid.ts is in no draft_paths. The wave and shatter terms also layer on top of instance matrices computed on the CPU each frame (cubeGrid.ts:96-122), and the clone's uniforms and program cache key are unspecified.
findings.suggestion: Add cubeGrid.ts to S3 and expose a narrow material-swap or attach API. Define look.attach(grid) and call it from resize(). Add a unit and an e2e test that resizes the viewport with enhanced on and asserts dispose counts and no stale mesh.
findings.resolution: Changed: C6 CubeGrid.setMaterialOverride, and C3 attach(grid) re-called after resize rebuilds. cubeGrid.ts is in S3, with unit, integration and e2e resize tests.

findings.finding: The 60 fps floor (AC3, D3) is the riskiest requirement, but the plan does not de-risk it. The only gate sits after S2 (bloom, floor, fog). S3 (shader waves, shatter, particles) and S4 (camera) add cost with no fallback, because the opaque-emissive switch is defined 'before S3' and quality tiers are a non-goal. AC3 is manual, and its reference device (Q2) is non-blocking. No basic-mode fps baseline on that device is required, though the glass is already 1800+ double-sided transparent clearcoat instances (cubeGrid.ts:59-70). useThreeScene caps pixel ratio at 2, so the composer may run at 2x on HiDPI. O4 itself notes that 'overdraw is the dominant cost' is unverified.
findings.suggestion: Make Q2 blocking before S2. Record basic-mode fps on that device first. Require each slice (S2, S3, S4) to re-pass AC3 and pre-agree a cut list (particle count, shatter, pixel-ratio cap, opaque material) for a miss. Run the opaque-emissive spike in S2 so the glass-or-opaque decision rests on a measurement.
findings.resolution: Changed: AC3 needs basic fps recorded first, and every slice re-checks AC3. D10 sets the reference device and the cut list. The opaque spike moves into S2. Q2 confirmation is due before S2; it is non-blocking because D10 gives a default.

findings.finding: AC6 and K2 cannot detect the risk they name. The debug:viz 'cubes.out' probe is registered in useCubesScene.update and reports bass.pulse (useCubesScene.ts:101-108), a CPU-side envelope value. Adding a composer in the render path does not change it, so AC6 passes trivially in enhanced mode while giving false assurance about visual latency. A 16.7 ms tolerance is also small against run-to-run noise (p95 59-74 ms in the brief).
findings.suggestion: Reword AC6 as a regression check on the envelope (acceptable, but state that it is not render latency), and add a real render-latency proxy, for example frame-time p95 from PerformanceStats in both modes. Otherwise drop K2's reliance on it.
findings.resolution: Changed: AC6 is reworded as an envelope regression check plus a frame-time p95 check in both modes; K2 updated.

findings.finding: AC7 and the success metric treat the lazy chunk as outside the budget ('initial Total JS stays within budget'). But .size-limit.json:19-22 defines Total JS as every chunk in build/client/assets/*.js, including lazy ones. The new chunk (look, shaders, controls, store, loader) counts in full. The brief records no current headroom, and recent commits already had to raise the limit. No slice edits .size-limit.json, although AGENTS.md:189-195 requires budget changes in the same PR. It is also unconfirmed that the EffectComposer, UnrealBloomPass and OutputPass addons dedupe with the bass-ink chunk.
findings.suggestion: In S1, record the current gzip total and the delta after the loader and look skeleton. Define AC7 against the Total JS line and the 133 kB entry line separately. Plan an explicit limit bump in the slice that needs it, and check that the addons land in a shared chunk.
findings.resolution: Changed: AC7 splits the entry and Total JS lines and allows a same-PR limit raise with its reason. S1 measures the delta and checks addon sharing; .size-limit.json is added to S1; K8 added.

findings.finding: The camera dolly and orbit drift are 'layered on createOrbitView' with no mechanism. OrbitControls owns camera.position and recomputes it on update() (app/lib/three/orbitView.ts:25-45). A nudge written directly to the camera is overwritten or snapped whenever the user drags or zooms. The nudge also counts toward the 0.5 'view changed' threshold (orbitView.ts:5, 39-44), which can flip the reset-view button on by itself. reset() restores the default position while the nudge continues. When the camera is unlocked, behaviour is untested.
findings.suggestion: Apply the motion to a scene-root group or the camera view offset, not camera.position, so it stays independent of orbit state and the changed flag. Add a test with the camera unlocked and a user drag during playback.
findings.resolution: Changed: D11 applies motion to a scene-root group, never camera.position. S5 tests an unlocked drag.

findings.finding: The audio-frame contract and edge cases are thin. C4 types beatPhase and barPhase as number, but the hub snapshot has barPhase: number | undefined and a barLocked flag (app/features/audio/hub/types.ts:27-42). Waves and shatter keyed on a phase that is undefined, or on silence, a paused source, or analyser undefined (useCubesScene.ts:126), have no defined behaviour. All ACs assume audio playing, and there is no AC for silence, source change mid-session, or load failure beyond a notice with no test named for it.
findings.suggestion: Make C4 phases nullable with a documented fallback (for example, free-running or zero amplitude). Add an AC or test for no source, silence and a source switch with enhanced on, plus a test for the failed-load notice.
findings.resolution: Changed: C4 phases are nullable with barLocked, and zero amplitude is the fallback. AC9 covers no source, silence, an unlocked bar and a source switch, with tests including the failed-load notice.

findings.finding: AC2 says only 'the enhanced look renders ... with no console errors', and the e2e spec asserts one canvas and no errors. A silently black or washed-out canvas would pass. The existing look was hand-tuned for direct renderer output (LIGHT_SCALE, DISPLAY_GAMMA, ENVIRONMENT_INTENSITY in useCubesScene.ts:19-30), and the composer plus OutputPass changes tone-mapping and colour handling for transparent, non-depth-writing glass and a flashing background. The plan reduces this to 'tuning needed'. K4's GLSL string snapshots only freeze text and prove nothing about rendering.
findings.suggestion: Add a canvas-not-blank assertion and one enhanced visual baseline (or a pixel statistic check) to the e2e spec. State the colour-pipeline decision (tone mapping, output colour space) in S1. Replace the GLSL snapshot tests with uniform and compile smoke tests.
findings.resolution: Changed: AC2 adds pixel statistics and an enhanced visual baseline. The colour pipeline is decided in S1 (K7). GLSL tests are uniform and compile smoke tests.

findings.finding: Slice ordering leaves gaps. Bloom follows the bass flash from S2, but reduced-motion damping (AC8) only arrives in S4, so S2 and S3 can ship flash behaviour without it. S3 bundles onBeforeCompile material cloning, a shatter term, a particle shader and two re-measurements in one 'M' slice. The enhanced-only controls (S4) create a conditional ControlPanel path and a static CubesControlValues type (cubesControls.ts) that appear nowhere in the tests, and the failure notice placement in CubesPage is unspecified.
findings.suggestion: Move the reduced-motion factor into the C4 and fxState work in S2. Split S3 into waves and shatter, then particles. Add a test that the default settings panel is unchanged with the flag off and that hidden controls do not affect basic mode.
findings.resolution: Changed: the reduced-motion damper moves to S2. S3 is split into waves and shatter (S3) and particles (S4); camera and controls are S5, with a default-panel-unchanged test.

freeze_first.definition: useCubesScene({ ..., enhanced: boolean }) additive; false keeps today's render (no composer); toggling swaps the look in place through a ref, with no useThreeScene rebuild.

freeze_first.definition: { bands: Float32Array | null; bassFlash: number; beatPhase: number | null; barPhase: number | null; barLocked: boolean; dt: number }; cubesFxState.step(frame, reducedMotion, out) writes into a preallocated uniforms object; null phases or barLocked false give zero beat and bar amplitude.

freeze_first.name: CubeGrid material hook
freeze_first.definition: CubeGrid.setMaterialOverride(material: Material | null): void; null restores the grid's own glass material. The basic path never calls it.
